newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IOC PRAISES B.AIRES' OLYMPIC "CORRIDOR" BID FOR 2004.
newsitem.headline: IOC PRAISES B.AIRES' OLYMPIC "CORRIDOR" BID FOR 2004.

text.p: An International Olympic Committee delegation in Buenos Aires to evaluate its bid for the 2004 Games ended its visit Thursday with praise for the concept of an "Olympic Corridor" along the River Plate.

The city's hopes rest on a 14 km "Olympic Corridor" along the coastline which could host 24 of the current 28 Olympic disciplines near the city centre, in sports installations of which 75 percent already exist.

"We want to show recognition for the concept of the Olympic Corridor, though it needs some improvments from the environmental aspect," said Thomas Bach, the German head of the IOC's Evaluating Committee, speaking for the committee.
He decline to go into detail about these environmental shortcomings, but acknowldged "the race for the Olympics is not easy. That's why we always say it's like a marathon."

Buenos Aires, which bid unsuccessfully for the Games in 1936, 1944, 1956 and 1968, is competing against a strong field of 11 cities. The IOC will select four finalists by March 7 and choose the 2004 Olympic city in early September.
Boch, as a German Olympian, won the world fencing championship here in 1977. He diplomatically evaded a journalist's question about what changes he saw in the city after 19 years.

"All cities change and more so after 19 years. But I've noticed no changes in the food, something on which I don't agree with Madonna," said Bach, referring to the U.S. pop star's criticisms of Argentina's heavily beef-based diet.

The IOC delegation, which leaves Friday after three days in Buenos Aires, tried to dispel fears that the city and its nearby competitor in the 2004 bid, Brazil's Rio de Janeiro, would not both be allowed to be among the four finalists.
